text: Chitti and Chinni were twins. It was their sixth birthday. They were happy and excited because amma and appa had promised to buy a pet for them.
"Will it be a parrot?" wondered Chitti.
"But parrots are meant to fly Chitti," replied Chinni.
"A rabbit?" Chinni said with sparkling eyes.
"How about a dog?" said Chitti.
The twins danced round and round thinking of their pets.
They kept singing whatever came out of their mouth.
" Our dear little friend is coming
Is coming from the pet shop"
Amma was cooking delicacies for the special day. She too seemed to be excited about the pets and sang along. " Our dear little friend is..la la la"
In the evening, appa came home with a big box. When he opened, there was no parrot or rabbit or a dog but a fish bowl with three beautiful fish.
Chitti held amma's sari tightly and stood with her mouth wide open.
'Amma knew what was going to come. Why didn't she tell us?' she thought.
But did Chinni keep quiet? No. Not at all. She cried and cried.

A little later, appa said, "Chitti, Chinni, you are too little to take care of big pets. On your next birthday, you will get a bigger pet. I promise. Now you take care of these fish. See to it that they don't cry and change the water every three days."
The twins looked at amma who lovingly said, "They are great pets. I'm sure you'll like them girls."
They thought amma was happy that she didn't have to invest time in taking care of big pets.
For three days, Chitti and Chinni didn't go near the fish bowl.
Finally, on the fourth day, they stood near the fish bowl and looked at each other. It was time to change the water.
But the gold fish was trying to say something. It swam around and came back peering at the girls.
It seemed like it was trying to talk to the twins.
Chitti and Chinni looked into the glass bowl. What they saw was amazing! There was a tiny little baby fish, 'the fry' inside.
They would have cleaned the bowl without noticing.
They had saved a baby fish. They were so glad. When amma and appa came to know, they too were happy.
Since then, Chitti and Chinni took care of the fishes and loved them.
